reproduction_target: DomDiff, a supervised conditional discrete-diffusion framework for protein family domain boundary delineation and domain family classification. Computational reproduction target = the full ML pipeline described in Methods §4: Swiss-Prot and COG sequence acquisition + quality-control filtering, BIO-scheme label conversion and stratified 8:1:1 split, ESM2-650M sequence embedding, NetSurfP secondary-structure feature generation, a two-layer biLSTM coarse-prior module, training of the 12-block ResDilatedBlock conditional diffusion denoiser, 30-step inference sampling, ablation variants, baseline re-training (DeepDom, DNN-Dom, BLAST, DeepFam, DeepPPF, 3mer, ProtENN2), and the metric computation (MCC, IoU, top-k error, mAP, Kappa). No wet-lab component.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation, built from Methods §4.1-§4.6 prose. §4.2 conditional-embedding text is split into three steps (ESM2-650M, NetSurfP, biLSTM coarse prior) because they are three distinct model invocations. The 12-block diffusion architecture (§4.3.1), forward diffusion (§4.3.2) and training objective are folded into one training step; sampling (§4.3.3) is a separate step because it carries its own hyperparameter (30 fixed inference steps). All seven baseline methods of §4.5 are one step, since the prose gives them one uniform treatment ('hyperparameters set according to the code from the original authors'). Evaluation metric computation (§4.4.3) is one step. No wet-lab steps; W = 0.

steps.label: Swiss-Prot sequence + domain-annotation acquisition (https://www.uniprot.org/) and quality filtering: drop length <10, drop length >1000, drop families with <10 members, drop duplicate sequences across multiple families; result 25,329 sequences / 3,268 families

COG dataset acquisition (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/cog) processed 'using the same method', plus removal of sequences with >30% similarity; result 317,853 sequences / 3,768 conserved domain types
BIO-scheme residue-level label conversion with hierarchical family-id encoding (B-123 / I-123 / O) and stratified 8:1:1 train/validation/test split by protein-family distribution
Per-residue sequence embedding with the ESM2-650M protein language model (Lin et al. 2023), producing X_esm of dimension d_esm
Secondary-structure / physicochemical feature generation with the NetSurfP model (cited as NetSurfP-3.0, Hoie et al. 2022), producing structural vector of dimension d_struct
Two-layer stacked biLSTM coarse-grained prior module over ESM2 embeddings, emitting coarse logits X_coarse concatenated into X_condition

Training of the conditional discrete diffusion denoiser: 12 stacked ResDilatedBlocks (kernel 3, dilation 2^n mod 9, base channels 512, sinusoidal time-step embedding, multi-head cross-attention to X_condition, max positional length 4096); cosine noise schedule beta_start=0.0001, beta_end=0.8, s=0.008, T=50 training steps; focal-loss objective; AdamW lr 1e-4, batch size 12, max 50 epochs, gradient accumulation 5, early stopping when val loss fails to drop by >1e-4 for 10 epochs; 4x NVIDIA A100-40GB with HuggingFace Accelerate + DeepSpeed, bf16, Python 3.10 / PyTorch 2.3

Inference / conditional sampling: iterative reverse denoising from Gaussian/uniform label noise with 30 fixed inference steps (reported optimum at t=20 endpoint), cross-attention conditioning at each block

Baseline comparison methods re-trained and tested on the same splits: DeepDom, DNN-Dom, distribution-based division, BLAST, DeepFam, DeepPPF, 3mer-LR, ProtENN2; 'hyperparameters set according to the code from the original authors' plus an added early-stopping criterion (loss decrease <1e-4 for 10 epochs); single A100-40GB, Python 3.10 / PyTorch 2.3, no mixed precision
Ablation studies: (a) remove biLSTM coarse-prior module, (b) remove NetSurfP structural features, (c) replace generative head with a discriminative classifier; evaluated by MCC / IoU / MAE

Evaluation: greedy domain matching (highest-overlap pairing, matched predictions removed from pool), boundary MCC with +/-20 residue tolerance, IoU, single/multi-domain count MAE, and classification F1 / recall / accuracy / precision / Cohen's Kappa / top-k error / mAP-10..1000; test set stratified into five 200-residue length groups (41664 / 83727 / 39165 / 9639 / 3010 sequences)

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 6/11 (55%) steps reach RI at the prose ceiling; 5/11 cap at NI. The RI steps are the model-side ones (ESM2-650M embedding, NetSurfP features, biLSTM prior, diffusion training, sampling, ablations), which benefit from an unusually complete hyperparameter table (optimizer, lr, batch, epochs, early-stopping delta, gradient accumulation, beta_start/beta_end/cosine s, block count, channels, positional max length, training and inference step counts) plus a stated software environment (Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.3, bf16, HuggingFace Accelerate + DeepSpeed, 4x A100-40GB). Those are exact pins WITHOUT environment closure, so version is capped at 1 and no step can exceed RI at stage 1. The NI steps fail on version: the two database ingests carry no Swiss-Prot / COG release pin, the label-conversion and split step names no software and no random seed, the baseline re-training step gives neither repository URLs nor versions for the eight comparison methods, and the evaluation step names no metric library. A stage-2 code read could in principle lift the six RI steps, but the declared repository is currently unresolvable (HTTP 404), so there is no artifact to read.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (sections 4.1-4.6). 0 wet-lab steps; this is a pure-computational methods/tool paper. A Code availability section is present (section 4.6); no Data availability section is present, though the two source databases are given as bare URLs inline in section 4.1.

gaps.where: Section 4.6 Code availability; all DomDiff-specific steps (C6, C7, C8, C10) and the preprocessing/evaluation scripts (C1, C2, C3, C11)
gaps.missing: The paper states verbatim: 'The DomDiff codebase is publicly available at https://github.com/zhangchao162/DomDiff.git'. That repository does not resolve at assessment time (GitHub web 404, GitHub REST API returns {"message":"Not Found"}). No mirror, Zenodo DOI, Software Heritage identifier, or release tag is given. There is therefore no readable code artifact, no README, and no landing page for stage-2 to inspect.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the repository (or make it public if private), and archive a tagged release to Zenodo / Software Heritage with a DOI cited in the Code availability section so the link does not depend on a mutable GitHub namespace.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 11 steps (section 4.4.1 and 4.5)
gaps.missing: The environment is stated only as prose pins: 'Python 3.10 and PyTorch 2.3', 'HuggingFace Accelerate and DeepSpeed frameworks', 'bf16 precision', '4 NVIDIA A100-40 GB GPUs'. No requirements.txt, conda environment file, conda-lock / pixi.lock / uv.lock, Dockerfile, or container digest is claimed anywhere. Accelerate, DeepSpeed, transformers, fair-esm, and NetSurfP are unversioned. PyTorch '2.3' is a minor-series pin, not a patch pin, and no CUDA / cuDNN version is given.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a lockfile (conda-lock or uv.lock) or a container image referenced by digest, covering Python, PyTorch + CUDA, Accelerate, DeepSpeed, the ESM2 loader, and NetSurfP.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C3 - Swiss-Prot and COG ingest and the derived training corpus
gaps.missing: No release version or download date for Swiss-Prot (given only as https://www.uniprot.org/) or for COG (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/cog). Both are rolling resources, so the stated post-filter counts (25,329 sequences / 3,268 families for Swiss-Prot; 317,853 sequences / 3,768 domain types for COG) are not re-derivable. The derived BIO-labelled corpus and the 8:1:1 stratified split are not deposited to any accession (no Zenodo / figshare / GEO-style identifier appears anywhere in the paper), and no random seed is given for the stratified sampling.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the Swiss-Prot release (e.g. UniProt 2025_03) and the COG release/date, deposit the filtered FASTA + BIO label files and the exact train/validation/test split indices to Zenodo or figshare, and record the split seed.

gaps.where: C2 similarity filtering; C5 NetSurfP invocation; C6 biLSTM sizing; C9 baseline hyperparameters
gaps.missing: C2: the >30% similarity removal names no tool (CD-HIT? MMseqs2? BLAST?), no identity definition, no coverage threshold, and no word-size/cluster settings. C5: no NetSurfP version string in the body (only the reference title says 3.0), no run mode, and no output-feature selection. C6: biLSTM hidden dimension, dropout, and the coarse-logit output dimension are unstated; d_esm and d_struct are symbolic. C9: baseline hyperparameters are deferred wholesale to 'the code from the original authors' with no repository URLs, commits, or per-method settings, and the added early-stopping rule is the only stated deviation.
gaps.how_to_close: State the similarity-reduction tool with exact parameters; give NetSurfP version and invocation; give the biLSTM layer dimensions and all symbolic dimensions numerically; list the baseline repositories with commit hashes and any per-method configuration deltas.

gaps.where: C3, C7, C8, C9 - stochastic components
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported for the stratified split, for weight initialisation, for the forward-diffusion label corruption (which draws u ~ Uniform[0,1] per residue per step), or for the reverse sampling from noise. Multi-GPU DeepSpeed training with bf16 is additionally nondeterministic by default; no determinism flags or repeat-run variance are reported.
gaps.how_to_close: Report and set seeds for split, initialisation, forward corruption, and sampling; state whether deterministic kernels were enabled; report metric variance over repeated runs or seeds.

gaps.missing: The Results section stratifies the test set into five length groups totalling 177,205 sequences, which cannot be a 10% test split of the 25,329-sequence Swiss-Prot corpus described in section 4.1 (nor of the 317,853-sequence COG corpus at 10%). The prose does not state which corpus each reported table/figure derives from, so the reported numbers cannot be attributed to a defined input without the code.
gaps.how_to_close: State explicitly, per table and figure, which dataset and which split the reported numbers come from, and reconcile the length-group counts with the stated corpus sizes.

gaps.missing: No trained DomDiff checkpoint is offered (the only availability statement is the 404 code repository), and the ESM2-650M checkpoint is identified by model-size name only, with no source URL, revision, or file hash.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the trained DomDiff weights alongside the code archive, and pin the ESM2-650M checkpoint by source and revision/hash.
